body.statement: For an observed law \(P\) satisfying known sequential randomization and \(e_h(a)\geq\varepsilon>0\) at every legal node-action pair, determine whether every \((q,\{U_h(k)\},\{V_{ha}(k)\})\in\mathcal R(P)\) has a single \(Q\in\mathfrak F(P)\) with \(q_Q=q\), including all dormant counterfactual branches and every joint consistency, randomization, reached-history modularity, and single-world product equality. The dormant-kernel extension lemma must then supply agreed \(\bar\kappa_{Q,v}\) versions on zero-probability fibers without changing \(Q\). If universal lifting fails, determine the smallest finite tree and the additional separating facet required for exact projection.
body.justification: This is the load-bearing local-to-global question; branchwise marginal preservation does not by itself construct a complete FFRCISTG response system, while null-fiber kernel agreement is handled separately by the extension lemma.
body.gap: FanPark2010 stops at a static pair of potential outcomes, while Shahn2026Oracle Appendix A couples incompatible branches but leaves the complete dormant-coordinate construction implicit and GreseleEtAl2022 demonstrates that causal marginals can have nontrivial global compatibility restrictions. The first specifically dynamic step not covered by the static result is to couple action-specific continuation maxima at every full history and glue those conditional couplings across descendants into one complete FFRCISTG system.
body.consumer: A positive resolution validates every sharpness and inference claim below; a negative resolution supplies the missing causal compatibility facet and prevents invalid SMART oracle bounds.
